title: Lost GET — Reporting and Recovery
body: One missed bucket tooth that rides a truck to the ROM pad and into the primary crusher turns into liner damage, days of plant downtime, and a stopped feed — all from something that costs nothing to catch at the loading face. At ADW that damage bill dwarfs the few minutes it takes to stop and check.
keyPoints: Stop first, ask questions second. Any suspected GET loss halts that machine immediately — don't finish the pass "just to be sure."
Isolate and report fast: supervisor cordons the area, logs time/location/GPS, and pulls in Survey, Drill & Blast, Load & Haul, and Safety together — not sequentially.
Track the material, not just the search. If it's not found on the spot, the muck's destination (pit → stockpile → ROM pad → crusher) gets documented and followed.
The ROM pad loader operator is the last line of defense — every load gets eyeballed for the missing piece before it reaches the crusher.
Prevention beats recovery: pre-start and daily GET checks, and training operators to recognize the feel/sound of a lost tooth, stop most of these before they start.
apply: Any excavator or loader working fresh muck near the crusher feed — a quick visual GET check before it starts loading is cheaper than an afternoon with the crusher down.
